# Content Focus

## Executive summary

### Core judgement

|  |
| --- |
| Public information shows that Kuailu Technology has built Kuailu Cloud, Kuailu Meeting and job smarts around "AI Smart Office" to cover sales, procurement, inventory, finance, personnel, administration, collaboration and meetings. Its main product characteristics can be summarized as: |
| ** Connects business operations and collaborative processes to the unified data base, adapts business through visualization and supports analysis, entry, alerting and implementation with AI. ** |
| Since the product is oriented towards enterprise procurement, the relevant users are not a single “consumer”, but rather a multi-player B2B decision-making and use system: business managers are concerned with business results, business owners are concerned with process efficiency, IT/information managers are concerned with integration, security and governance, finance/procurement is concerned with inputs and risks, ultimately shared by sales, procurement, warehousing, finance, personnel, administration and management. |
| The product structure and case studies of the integrated brand, with the following characteristics of the common adaptation organization: |
| (b) Cross-sectoral collaboration and data management complexity following the expansion of enterprises; |
| Spreadsheets, instant messaging and multiple business systems coexist, with duplicate entries or inconsistent data calibres; |
| Have quantifiable business processes such as sales, procurement, inventory, after-sale or cross-regional operations; |
| Concerned about data access, auditing, system integration or privatization deployment; |
| It is hoped that AI will be introduced from specific scenarios such as minutes of meetings, CRM, procurement or write-offs. |

### Core population structure

| Core population | Typical organization or workplace environment | Main focus | Corresponding product capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Business owners, general managers, managers | Growing-up manufacturing, trade, energy, medical equipment, renewable resources enterprises | Operational visualization, costs and cross-sectoral synergies | Operation of the cockpit, harmonization of data and cross-module processes |
| Chief of sales and operations | B2B enterprises with high-priced, long-sale, heavy sales | Customer deposition, process visualization and sales forecasting | AI CRM, Threads - Refunds - Sales closed ring |
| Chief of Procurement, Supply Chain, Warehouse | Multi-SKU, multi-supplier, multi-silo or price-volatile industries | Adjudication, accuracy of inventory, synergy and traceability | AI Procurement, write-offs, WMS |
| IT/Infomatic Officer | OA/ERP/CRM for enterprises that need integration or privatization | Safety, integration, authority and maintenance | Privatization deployment, API, visualization extension |
| Executive, conference management and high-frequency participants | Organizations across regions, across languages or that value the confidentiality of meetings | Stabilization conference, automatic summary and post-session implementation | Kuailu Meeting, AI Summary and To-do |
| Head of Human Rights, Finance, Administration, etc. | Management of SMEs that are still more dependent on manual forms | Process automation and reduction of duplication of effort | Personnel, finance and administration application templates |

### Purchase Driver Sorting

|  |
| --- |
| Integrated disclosure of product information, case studies and industry environment, with the purchasing motivations of the target clients generally following the following order: |
| ** Resolvable operational issues**: non-receivable stocks, black boxes in the sales process, slow approvals, double entry of data, no deposition of meetings; |
| ** Whether input output is clear**: how many people are saved, how many errors are reduced, how long do we get online, whether we can replace existing software costs; |
| **According to the enterprise process**: full system re-engineering is not required, visual configuration is iterative and industry templates can be rapidly adapted; |
| ** Whether data and systems support authority management and operation scarring**: authority, log, backup, privatization, innovation and compliance; |
| **The ability to coexist with existing systems**: ERP, finance, mainstream enterprise office platforms, mail, database and API connectivity; |
| **Whether the organization is really useful**: operational thresholds, mobile end experience, training, after-sales and continuous operation; |
| ** Credibility of suppliers and long-term service**: customer case, third-party certification, service team, version iterative and business stability. |

## Purchase drivers depth analysis

### Functional drivers

#### Driver I: Turn data into end-to-end business stream

|  |
| --- |
| Clients are usually not “no software”, but rather too many software, forms and chat tools. The real purchase objective is to reduce duplicate entries and allow sales, procurement, warehousing, finance and management to work around the same data. |
| Corresponding product values: harmonized data model, cross-module trigger, API/database connection, business questions. |

#### Driver II: Rapid adaptation to non-standardized processes

|  |
| --- |
| The systems and operations of growing enterprises are still changing, and the traditional ERP two is slow and expensive, and the purely standard cloud service is not very relevant. Visualization brings not “development for all” as a core value, but rather a change in business that does not wait in line for IT. |
| Corresponding product values: forms, processes, reports, portals, templates and custom operations. |

#### Driver III: Let AI move from "response to questions" to "implementation"

|  |
| --- |
| Businesses ' new sense of universal chat robots has declined and are more willing to pay for automatic filing, filling, generating quotations, triggering approvals, forecasting inventories and synchronizing assignments. |
| Corresponding product value: Job intelligence, AI CRM, procurement request price, meeting to-do, cross-system implementation. |

#### Driver IV: Security and control

|  |
| --- |
| Conference, client, contractual, financial and personnel data are sensitive. Privatization deployments, competencies, logs and enterprise-owned servers will significantly increase the willingness to monitor clients ' payments. |
| Corresponding product values: privatization, enterprise-level security, data segregation, logs, letter creation and certification. |

#### Driver V: Cross-regional collaboration with weak networks

|  |
| --- |
| For cross-border trade, overseas branches, factories and remote service teams, multilingual, real-time captioning, standardized documentation and low-bandwidth meetings are business continuity requirements rather than mere optimization. |

### Economic drivers

|  |
| --- |
| Reducing the cost of multiple software subscriptions and interface maintenance; |
| (b) Reduction in the capacity of reporting, recording, checking, summary and reminder staff; |
| Reducing stock backlogs, stock shortages, procurement price differentials and payment errors; |
| Shortening the sales, approval, delivery and recovery cycles; |
| One-time customized development with subscription and visual configuration alternatives; |
| Reducing the cost of digital failure through sector pilots. |
| The really valid ROI formula should read: |
| ** Annualization gain = time cost saving + error/loss reduction + turnover and conversion improvement - software subscription - implementation and integration - training and migration - ongoing ** |

### Emotional and identity dynamics

|  |
| --- |
| Enterprise software purchases are not entirely rational and include the following: |
| The boss wants to move from “person-to-person” to “data pipe”; |
| The manager wishes to demonstrate, at the request of the board or consortium, that AI has produced operational results; |
| IT wants to move away from endless and sporadic development needs; |
| Chiefs of operations want to reduce cross-sectoral privation and increase controllability; |
| The employee wants to get rid of repeated work but fears being monitored or replaced by AI. |
| The acceptance of AI by relevant actors is often influenced by both a “advanced sense” and a “safe sense of security” and by concerns about controllability, auditability and traceability. |

### Social and policy drivers

|  |
| --- |
| Sectors such as the Ministry of Industry and Communications have promoted the digital transformation of SMEs, explicitly requiring the provision of “small and light” solutions around “resistance to turn, afraid to turn, unable to turn”, with emphasis on downside, efficiency gains, safety and industry suitability. |
| [Source: Ministry of Industry and Communications, 2025 Pilot Notification] (https://www.miit.gov.cn/xwfb/gxdt/sjdt/art/2025/art_2764fad98e3f45b5af7e1258a8cdbf8d.html) |
| Policies provide a market environment for low-cost, rapid deployment and industry-appropriate digital products. The actual purchasing judgement of the enterprise remains linked to business effectiveness, conditions of implementation and service capacity. |
